Introduction | 01

Introduction | Rock | - | paper | - | scissors | is | a | classic | game | . | Its | main | purpose | is | to | resolve | disputes | . | Because | the | three | players | are | mutually | restrained, | there | will | always | be | a | winner | no | matter | how | many | times | a | tie | occurs | . | The | rock | - | paper | - | scissors | game | can | determine | the | winner | by | using | only | three | gestures | : | scissors, | rock, | and | paper | . | In | the | process | of | rock | - | paper | - | scissors, | at | least | two | people | must | participate | to | determine | the | winner | . | In | the | JDPH¶V | rules, | rock | beats | scissors, | scissors | beats | paper, | and | paper | beats | rock | .
New Knowledge | 02

The origin of the rock | - | paper | - | scissors game | There | are | two | theories | about | its | origin | : | one | is | that | it | originated | in | China, | mainly | from | the | "Wu | Za | Zu" | written | by | people | in | the | Ming | Dynasty, | which | records | that | the | earliest | rock | - | paper | - | scissors | originated | from | the | hand | gestures | and | fist | - | fighting | of | the | Han | Dynasty | . | Another | theory | is | that | it | originated | in | Japan | in | the | 19 | th | century | . | In | the | 20 | th | century, | the | game | of | rock | - | paper | - | scissors | began | to | spread | to | Europe | and | the | United | States | . | Europe | and | the | United | States | called | it | the | "Japanese | game," | and | the | French | called | it | "jeu | Japonais" | (meaning | Japanese | game) | .

A psychological analysis of this game | "Rock, | Paper, | Scissors" | is | actually | a | psychological | game, | especially | when | you | first | play, | it | has | a | lot | to | do | with | your | psychological | personality | . | Like | to | play | "Rock" | - | Strong | adaptability | ; | aggressive | Like | to | play | "Paper" | - | Strong | control | desire, | good | at | socializing, | and | often | easy | to | get | wealth | . | Like | to | play | "Scissors" | - | Lack | of | security

Further Reading | Some | researchers | have | discovered | a | winning | strategy | for | rock | - | paper | - | scissors | through | experiments | . | The | researchers | recruited | 360 | students, | divided | them | into | six | groups, | and | randomly | paired | them | to | play | 300 | rounds | of | rock | - | paper | - | scissors | games | . | The | students | who | won | each | round | would | receive | a | small | amount | of | RMB | reward | . | By | observing | the | strategies | used | by | the | students, | they | found | the | game | strategies | that | winners | or | losers | usually | use | : | if | you | are | a | loser, | switch | to | a | move | that | can | defeat | your | opponent | in | the | next | round | ; | if | you | are | a | winner, | do | not | use | the | original | move | in | the | next | round | . | In | other | words, | if | you | beat | your | opponent's | scissors | with | rock, | then | you | can | no | longer | use | rock | in | the | next | round, | but | scissors, | because | the | opponent | is | likely | to | use | paper | .
